PROJECT OVERVIEW

Rethinking what frozen dessert can feel like.

Frozen dessert often sits between two extremes: indulgent but guilt-driven, or better-for-you but stripped of pleasure. Nouri explores a third position, combining appetite appeal, considered design and honest communication.

The challenge was balancing warmth with restraint. Too playful and the brand loses its premium character; too minimal and it becomes cold. Typography, colour, packaging and photography were developed together to create an identity that feels both inviting and refined.

"How do you make indulgence feel like a considered choice rather than a guilty one?"

BRAND STRATEGY

A brand built around thoughtful indulgence.

01

BRAND IDEA

Indulgence, reconsidered.

Nouri treats pleasure and nourishment as complementary rather than competing ideas. The product should feel desirable first, with its nutritional qualities supporting the experience rather than defining it.

02

POSITIONING

Premium frozen dessert for people who think about what they eat without making it a performance.

Nouri sits between everyday supermarket ice cream and highly artisanal dessert brands: elevated and intentional, without becoming precious.

03

BRAND PROMISE

"Delicious first. Nourishing always."

Pleasure leads the experience. Nutrition provides the proof. The brand never needs health language to make the product desirable.

04

BRAND PERSONALITY

Warm without being playful. Premium without being austere. Honest without being clinical.

PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

The product informed the brand.

Nouri was developed beyond its visual identity. A concept formulation for Mango Bliss helped ground decisions around positioning, packaging hierarchy and communication in an actual product rather than hypothetical claims.

CONCEPT FORMULATION · Requires laboratory verification before commercial production

Mango Bliss lead flavour

FORMULATION V2.1

Mango Bliss was developed as the lead flavour, using mango purée as the primary flavour and colour source. The formulation balances fruit, dairy protein, cream, fibre and sweetness to create a dessert concept that still prioritises taste and texture. This product thinking helped define what Nouri could credibly communicate on pack, rather than designing claims first and building the product around them.

The recipe keeps the finish clean and scoopable, with enough protein to feel purposeful and enough sweetness to stay indulgent. It feels like a premium dessert first, and a better-for-you option second.

What the formulation supports

CLAIMS

Nouri’s nutritional messaging was developed from the formulation rather than added as a marketing layer. Protein contributes to structure, fibre supports body, and sweetness was balanced with texture and flavour in mind.

This gave the brand a credible foundation for communicating nutritional benefits without allowing them to define the product.

The claims are proof, not the pitch.

"High protein"available

27.8% of energy from protein. Available and defensible - held across V2 and V2.1.

"Low fat"available

2.5 g per 100 g, with 0.5 g margin above the 3 g threshold.

"Source of fibre"available

3.6 g vs. 3 g threshold - now a real margin, not a marginal one. Use AOAC 2001.03 for analysis.

"No added sugar"not available

Sucrose is added. "Reduced sugar" qualifies; "no added sugar" does not.

"Guilt-free", "naturally healthy"avoid

Not permitted health claims. They also contradict the brand's own voice.

Product claims are intentionally presented as a clear consumer story, not a legal or regulatory assessment.

ART DIRECTION

Photography carries the appetite appeal.

The photography direction was built around three modes: texture macro, ingredient stills and product in context. Each has a specific role. Together they carry warmth and appetite appeal in ways that typography and colour cannot do alone.

Three photography modes

DIRECTION

TEXTURE MACRO

Close views of the dessert surface communicate richness and quality before the customer reads a word.

INGREDIENT STILLS

Single ingredients on clean backgrounds communicate what is inside with minimal decoration.

PRODUCT IN CONTEXT

The product appears in environments that feel premium but unpretentious, prioritising surface, light and proportion over excessive styling.

PHOTOGRAPHY PRINCIPLES

Asymmetric crops

Off-centre compositions and deliberate negative space keep the imagery editorial rather than catalogue-like.

Natural directional light

Single-direction lighting creates depth, warmth and tactile contrast.

Tactile surfaces

Stone, wood and linen give the imagery a tactile, grounded quality.

Appetite first

The product should look desirable before any nutritional message enters the conversation.

DESIGN SYSTEM

A system designed to stay recognizable.

Nouri was designed as a scalable system. The same core rules can support new flavours, formats and applications without losing the brand's identity.

COLOUR

One flavour family per variant, supported by a shared neutral core and defined type contrast.

TYPOGRAPHY

Vollkorn creates character, Hanken Grotesk handles supporting copy, and IBM Plex Mono separates product data.

GRAPHIC

Wrap and Accent Tick provide a consistent visual structure across packaging and brand applications.

WORDMARK

Used primarily in Ink on light backgrounds and reversed in Ivory on dark backgrounds.

NEUTRAL CORE

Oat, Ivory and Ink anchor the identity while supporting tones create hierarchy across layouts.

EXTENDING TO NEW FLAVOURS

A new flavour enters the system through a Field, Deep and Tint palette, a defined type contrast, and the established packaging structure. The identity can expand without changing its core rules.

REFLECTION

Designing the system, not just the package.

01

IDENTITY AS A SYSTEM

Nouri changed how I think about brand identity. Typography, colour, photography and packaging became more valuable when I stopped treating them as separate assets and started designing the relationships between them.

02

DESIGNING AT REAL SCALE

Working on the packaging changed how I think about hierarchy. What reads clearly on a screen does not automatically work on a tub or from a distance. Designing at real scale forced me to decide which elements deserved attention and which could be removed.

03

BALANCING APPETITE AND RESTRAINT

The hardest part was making Nouri feel warm without becoming playful and premium without becoming cold. No single design choice solved that tension. The result came from getting typography, imagery, colour, whitespace and tone to reinforce one another.
